description: Team Dhruvatara presents MARSWALK for the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge. MARSWALK is an AI-powered terrain analysis and mission-planning platform. Integrating NASA imagery and elevation data, it helps users optimize exploration routes, identify hazards, estimate resources, and plan rover operations. We emphasize scientific accuracy to make Mars exploration informed, efficient, and resilient.
summary:
MARSWALK is a browser-based mission planning and hazard perception platform designed to optimize planetary rover navigation, energy budgeting, and traversability validation across Martian terrain. Hosted on AWS EC2 with a FastAPI, Rasterio, and React architecture, it replaces heavy 16–30 GB desktop GIS suites with a zero-installation cloud workspace.

Grounded in official NASA datasets—including Mars Trek Jezero NE Syrtis Midway Digital Elevation Models, Visible Mosaics, and Curiosity’s AI4MARS imagery—MARSWALK integrates three core capabilities:

Multi-Strategy Route Planning: Using A* and Dijkstra algorithms over multi-layered elevation grids, operators compute and compare Shortest, Safest, Energy-Efficient, and Balanced trajectories while enforcing configurable slope limits.

Physics-Informed Mission Simulation: Models outbound and return drives using rover mass, battery capacity, rolling resistance, and tilt thresholds to quantify watt-hour draw, while Google Gemini AI translates raw telemetry into clear engineering risk summaries and go/no-go recommendations.

Deep Learning Visual Perception: A custom PyTorch U-Net model (92.95% test accuracy) segments surface camera frames into pixel-wise hazard masks for Soil, Bedrock, Sand, and Big Rock.

Validated on Jezero Crater data, MARSWALK’s modular architecture is readily adaptable to upcoming NASA Artemis lunar south pole missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

MARSWALK is an integrated, browser-based planetary rover mission planning, terrain intelligence, and autonomous hazard perception platform. It enables mission operators and researchers to model, validate, and stress-test safe, energy-efficient routes across Martian terrain prior to physical surface drives through three core modules:

  • Multi-Strategy Rover Route Planner: Processes NASA Mars Trek Jezero NE Syrtis Midway Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and Visible Mosaics using A* and Dijkstra graph-search algorithms. Operators can generate and visually compare four trajectories simultaneously—Shortest, Safest, Energy-Efficient, and Balanced—while enforcing configurable rover slope limits and hazard boundaries.
  • Physics-Informed Mission Planner: Simulates complete outbound and return drive profiles based on realistic vehicle parameters (mass, battery capacity, rolling resistance coefficients, and maximum tilt thresholds). It flags slope violations, calculates cumulative energy draw in watt-hours, and integrates Google Gemini AI to convert raw numerical telemetry into structured engineering assessments, risk summaries, and go/no-go recommendations.
  • AI Terrain Intelligence: Uses a custom PyTorch U-Net semantic segmentation model trained on NASA’s AI4MARS Curiosity imagery (achieving 92.95% test accuracy) to classify surface camera frames into pixel-wise hazard masks across four categories: Soil, Bedrock, Sand (entrapment risk), and Big Rock (collision obstacle).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Eliminates Hardware Barriers: Traditional planetary GIS workflows require downloading and processing 16–30 GB datasets on high-end workstations. MARSWALK delivers real-time raster pathfinding and neural network inference directly in any standard web browser with zero local installation.
  • Unified Decision Support: Bridges the gap between macro-scale orbital route planning and micro-scale surface hazard perception while translating complex physics telemetry into immediate, actionable operator insights.
  • Cross-Mission Extensibility: While validated on NASA Jezero Crater data, MARSWALK’s modular geospatial and perception architecture is designed to scale directly to upcoming lunar south pole operations under the NASA Artemis program.

Tools, Languages, Software & Infrastructure

  • Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript / TypeScript
  • Backend & Geospatial Processing: FastAPI (asynchronous API), Rasterio (DEM elevation and slope raster processing), NumPy
  • Frontend & Visualization: React interactive map interface
  • AI & Machine Learning: PyTorch (custom U-Net semantic segmentation), Google Gemini API (automated telemetry reasoning and risk reporting)
  • Cloud Infrastructure: Amazon Web Services (AWS EC2)
  • Official NASA Datasets: NASA Mars Trek Jezero NE Syrtis Midway DEM & Visible Mosaic (MRO HiRISE, CTX, HRSC), NASA AI4MARS Dataset (Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity)

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Creativity: Instead of treating orbital pathfinding, physical energy modeling, surface computer vision, and telemetry reporting as isolated tools, MARSWALK unifies them into a single, zero-footprint web platform—pairing classical physics-informed graph search with deep learning vision and generative AI engineering summaries.
    • Rover Safety & Mechanics: Enforced hard tilt constraints and differentiated terrain rolling resistance to prevent wheel entrapment in sand or high-centering on boulders.
    • Energy Budgeting: Accounted for gravitational potential energy changes across elevation deltas on both outbound and return legs to ensure battery margins remain viable.
    • Accessibility & Latency: Engineered an asynchronous cloud backend on AWS EC2 to handle heavy raster computations and deep learning inference smoothly for browser clients without specialized hardware.
